title: React Router DOM hooks
summary: Three React Router hooks: useParams reads values from the URL (like the 25 in /pokemon/25), useNavigate changes pages from code (after a click or a form submit), and useOutletContext shares state from the layout to its pages so you avoid prop drilling and keep state when switching pages. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Build a details page from a URL parameter, navigate from code, and share layout state with useOutletContext.

steps.title: Read both lessons
steps.detail: Read 'useNavigate and useParams' and 'useOutletContext', especially 'What is Prop Drilling?' and 'The Problem: State Resets on Page Navigation'.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain prop drilling in one sentence.

steps.title: Add a dynamic route
steps.detail: In your scratch router app from FE 6, add this child route and page from the lesson, then visit /pokemon/25.

steps.title: Share state through the Outlet
steps.detail: Move a piece of state into App.jsx, pass it with <Outlet context={{ favorites, setFavorites }} />, and read it in a page with useOutletContext(). Then switch pages and come back.
steps.doneWhen: The state survives switching between pages.

steps.title: Map it onto Myflix
steps.detail: In Myflix, ShowModal opens a title using openId state. Write down how /title/:id with useParams and useNavigate could replace that, and which state (like My List) would go in Outlet context. Plan only; check what the Netflix clone assignment asks first.
steps.doneWhen: You have a short plan naming the route, the param, and the shared state.

concepts.meaning: A changing part of a path, like :id in /title/:id.
Hook that returns the URL parameters for the current route.
Hook that gives you a function to change pages from code.
Passing props through components that don't use them just to reach a deeper one.
Hook that reads the value a layout passed to <Outlet context={...} />.
